title: Selective effects of selenium substitution on superconductivity and magnetic memory in 4Hb-TaS2
authors: Shalev Gur, Sajilesh K. P., Shubam Purwar, Irena Feldman, Ilay Mangel, Nitzan Ragoler, Amit Kanigel, Beena Kalisky
abstract: Disorder plays a central role in correlated quantum materials, but its effects can be highly selective when several electronic orders coexist. The van der Waals heterostructure 4Hb-TaS2 provides such a case, combining superconductivity, charge-order tendencies, strong scattering, and magnetic memory manifested through spontaneous vortices. Here we use Se substitution as a controlled local perturbation of the disorder landscape in 4Hb-TaS2. We find that superconductivity remains remarkably robust while the magnetic memory is strongly suppressed at higher Se concentrations. These results show that Se substitution does not create the hidden magnetic memory, but instead selectively weakens its macroscopic manifestation. More broadly, they reveal a sharp separation between robust superconducting and hidden-memory phases, and a highly disorder-sensitive spontaneous-vortex response in 4Hb-TaS2.
summary: This experimental work examines the effect of Selenium substitution on the correlated material 4Hb-TaS2, which exhibits both superconductivity and magnetic memory. The key finding is that while superconductivity remains remarkably robust against Se doping, the spontaneous magnetic memory effect is rapidly suppressed. This suggests a selective coupling mechanism where the disorder primarily impacts the hidden magnetic state rather than the superconducting pairing itself.
main_problem: The study investigates how substituting Selenium (Se) into the van der Waals heterostructure 4Hb-TaS2 selectively affects its superconductivity and a coexisting magnetic memory effect.
main_result: Se substitution robustly maintains superconductivity ($T_c$ and RRR are largely unchanged) while strongly suppressing the macroscopic manifestation of the magnetic memory effect.
method: The researchers used controlled Se substitution via synthesis and employed advanced SQUID microscopy to probe local magnetic flux and quantify spontaneous vortices associated with the memory effect.
model_or_system: The physical system is the van der Waals heterostructure 4Hb-TaS2, which exhibits unconventional superconductivity alongside charge-order tendencies and a magnetic memory effect characterized by spontaneous vortices.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$), Residual-Resistance Ratio (RRR), and the density/strength of spontaneous magnetic vortices.
important_parameters: Se substitution concentration ($x$), the characteristic temperature for memory loss ($T^*$), and the superconducting critical temperature ($T_c$).
main_assumptions: The substitution is treated as a controlled local perturbation of the disorder landscape, and the memory effect is hypothesized to be linked to the intrinsic incommensurate/CDW landscape.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the memory-probing protocol comparing zero-field vs. field-cooled states, showing the suppression of spontaneous vortices with increasing Se concentration, while $T_c$ and RRR remain relatively stable.
paper_structure: The paper systematically measures transport properties ($T_c$, RRR) and magnetic response (vortex counting) across a series of Se-substituted samples, contrasting the stability of the superconducting state against the sensitivity of the magnetic memory.
why_interesting: The sharp decoupling observed between the robust superconducting phase and the highly sensitive magnetic memory phase provides a model for understanding how different emergent quantum orders can coexist and respond differently to external perturbations.
